overall: The AG declined to review convening-procedure claims as untimely, found the complaint timely for the rest, and found no Open Meeting Law violation on the Purpose 1, minutes-detail, and records-listing allegations. No order issued.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board failed to follow required procedures before convening in its August 4, 2020 executive session.
allegations.key_passage: Any allegations regarding the Board’s convening procedures before entering executive session were discoverable on August 4, 2020, and therefore any complaint regarding these procedures should have been filed within 30 days of August 4, 2020.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board 'abused' Purpose 1 (reputation/discipline of individuals) by discussing an elected member and complaints it deemed meritless, without reading subject rights into the record.
allegations.key_passage: Additionally, the Open Meeting Law does not speak to or restrict what conduct may form the basis of a complaint that may be discussed in executive session under Purpose 1.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the minutes of the August 4, 2020 executive session were insufficient in detail and accuracy.
allegations.key_passage: After review of the minutes of the Board’s August 4, 2020, executive session, we find that they meet this standard and are sufficiently detailed.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the executive session minutes failed to list the records used at the meeting, and should say if none were used.
allegations.key_passage: After review, we do not find evidence that any documents were used during the meeting.
